data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 frames the comparison as conditional (decentralized is more resilient 'only when' a demonstrable causal independence barrier exists) and defers to 'the number of services N is a red herring' in favor of causal-graph diversity. But the problem asks to argue for or against the specific claim comparing a decentralized network of small services to ONE LARGE SERVICE with strictly more total internal redundancy. By sidelining the total-internal-redundancy dimension, SRC_002 avoids the hardest adversarial case: a monolith whose internal redundancy is heterogeneous across causally-isolated failure domains. Its evidence standard (separate supply chains, codebases, teams, jurisdictions) is a sufficient condition for independence but is not the only way a single large service can achieve it, so it does not address whether the large redundant service could instantiate the same independence barrier internally.
